title: Welcome to U.A.
tone: Almost entirely fun. Orientation. The class is meeting each other, discovering the school is hard and also ridiculous. Ruin is a name everyone in Tokyo already recognises — background noise the class hasn't touched yet. Fracture, the separate anti-licensing movement getting louder across the city, hasn't either. Class 1-B is a name on a results board. By level 4, the students feel like a cohort — and the world should feel like it's about to ask something of them.
dm_overview: Every beat in Tier 1 comes straight off the character sheets — Ren going missing mid-sprint because Overclock genuinely moves too fast to track, Chozen's Stress activating on its own in round one because it doesn't ask permission, Nakaya short-circuiting the common room toaster and refusing to apologize for it. Nothing here draws blood that matters. The entrance exam's danger is embarrassment in front of nineteen strangers, not injury; the worst outcome of Capture the Flag is losing to Yoshibara's clones and hearing about it from Masahata's fridge chart for a week. That changes starting Tier 2.

arcs.name: The Entrance Exam
arcs.summary: A staged disaster scenario in a simulated city block. Rescue civilians (actors), destroy drones (points), survive to the results board. The last wave is a boss drone nobody can solo — the class's first forced cooperation moment.
arcs.dm_setup: This is the first time these twenty characters are in a room together. Oshiro's PA cuts in with three flat sentences and no countdown — 'Simulated urban rescue scenario. Exam begins now.' — and then it's just noise: drone hatches opening, a building facade coming down, civilian actors shouting for help. There's no stated win condition beyond doing well, so nobody's coordinating, everybody's improvising, and the first real information about who these people are shows up in what they do in the first thirty seconds, not their final score.

major_beats.name: The Whistle
major_beats.description: Oshiro's PA cuts in with no countdown: 'Simulated urban rescue scenario. Exam begins now.' Drone hatches open. A building facade collapses (safe, loud). Civilian actors start shouting.
major_beats.dm_notes: Don't give players time to plan. Let the instinct reads happen naturally.

player_hooks.ren: Gone before anyone registers he moved — Overclock's faint blue vein-lines are the only trace, and even those are hard to catch. Other students will ask where he went. Let them wonder.
player_hooks.chozen: This is loud, chaotic, and stressful, and his Stress quirk doesn't ask permission — it just reads the environment. A tremor of unwanted activation (visible vein-darkening across his neck) hits him in round 1 before he's decided to fight anything. He didn't choose this. He's already thought through what to do about it, because he's already thought through everything, but 'plan for accidental activation during a school exam' wasn't on the list he made at home.
player_hooks.kazama: Hardens immediately and wades straight into drone fire — no civilians at risk from him the way a blaster's stray shot would be, so close range is simply the safe option for everyone else. His steel catches the exam lighting with that unusual mirror-bright sheen instead of the dull grey most Steel users show. He doesn't think about why. Nobody's ever told him it's unusual.
player_hooks.izuto: Needs a beat before he's at full output — the engine components on his calves have to spin up. He's noticeably behind in round 1, which he hates, and is already doing mental maintenance math about how much 'juice' this exam is going to cost him before it's even started.

major_beats.name: First Contact
major_beats.description: Mk.I drone wave, 2-3 at a time, targeting nearest student. Real-time scoreboard visible in the arena.
major_beats.dm_notes: Character dynamics emerge from the point competition, not from the DM forcing it.

player_hooks.masahata: Has been mentally ranking optimal drone routes since the PA announcement ended. His family ranks things at the dinner table as a matter of course; this is just Tuesday to him. He announces his running total out loud, unprompted, to nobody in particular.
player_hooks.aikawa: First to charge anything. She's wanted this exact moment since she was six years old and watched a rescue on the news — this is not a metaphor, she has said this out loud to at least four people already today. Claws out, in close, loud about it.
player_hooks.yoshibara: Doubles herself the second she registers 'more targets = more points.' Someone bumps into the double mid-fight and is visibly startled that it's a few degrees colder than skin should be. Oshiro notes this — not the doubling, the fact that she thought of it first.
player_hooks.toshida: A shout escapes mid-exam and a wall segment goes down. Civilian actors run from the falling wall, not the drones. Somehow this still nets rescue points.

major_beats.name: The Civilian Problem
major_beats.description: Civilian actors are scattered through the arena, 'endangered' by drones and debris. Rescuing scores triple — but costs combat time.
major_beats.dm_notes: First values test. No wrong answer between rescuing and fighting — the split should generate real in-character friction.

player_hooks.chozen: The panic and noise around a trapped civilian actor spikes his stress in a way he didn't plan for — he crosses into a low-grade activation without deciding to, faint darkening along his forearms. He gets the civilian clear fine. He also spends the next ten minutes annoyed that his body did something before he told it to.
player_hooks.izuto: Excellent at moving civilians fast and safely — this is exactly what Engine is for, and he knows it without needing to be told. Let him be quietly, competently good at this.
player_hooks.setaka: Physically carries two actors out under each arm without breaking stride, then apologises to both of them for the indignity of being carried. One of them tries to give him their contact info afterward, mistaking him for a real hero already. He writes their name down. He will actually send that thank-you note later.

major_beats.name: The Sentinel Arrives
major_beats.description: Boss drone drops when Oshiro judges the class has spent enough time working solo. Suppression Field goes up immediately — everyone feels the ground start to resist.
major_beats.dm_notes: Don't engineer the cooperation moment — let it emerge. If they don't coordinate, the Sentinel grinds them down slowly. When they do, make the Phase Armour breaking at 40 HP feel like a genuine turn.

player_hooks.ren: Fast enough to reach any angle of the Suppression Field, but the field itself drags at him — his first real experience of a mobility limit that isn't about how fast he can go.
player_hooks.kazama: The field slows him down like everyone else, but doesn't stop him closing distance and hardening up directly against the drone. First time this exam he's had to grind instead of finishing something clean.
player_hooks.chozen: The Sentinel is a machine. It has no fear response, no stress of its own for him to key off, and the fight itself is stressful enough on its own terms — which means by the time Phase Armour cracks, he's running hotter than he expected to be this early in his first day.
player_hooks.izuto: Burning through 'juice' faster than he budgeted for, fighting the field's drag. First real lesson in what the reserve actually costs him.

major_beats.name: The Result Board
major_beats.description: Scores posted. All students pass. Individual rankings go up. Masahata has a notebook open before Oshiro finishes reading.
major_beats.dm_notes: Read scores in Oshiro's voice: flat, alphabetical, no commentary. The class will editorialise themselves. Also shows Class 1-B's top score in a second column: Yamaru Todao, 84 pts.

player_hooks.masahata: Announces his own score before Oshiro finishes reading it. The class is already tired of him. It's session one. This is correct.
player_hooks.ren: High drone count, low civilian rescues — the miss is obvious in hindsight. He shrugs it off out loud. Oshiro writes something down and doesn't share it.

minor_beats: Kinosho is found asleep on a rooftop nobody saw her climb, in the top 5 regardless. When Neutralization actually activates near the end, her eyes flatten to a dull pewter grey for a second before colour drains back in — the first time most of the class sees it happen. Someone will eventually call this 'turning off.'
Nakaya tries to short a Mk.I drone's targeting system with a controlled arc — drone safety protocols eject her ten feet. She's fine. She's delighted. She scores the point anyway.

Ando's scales shrug off a glancing drone hit and he immediately turns it into a bit for the nearest classmate — the sunglasses do not come off even once, including for the part where a drone detonation goes off directly behind him and everyone sees him flinch first and joke second.

Ichitaka doesn't chase points. He projects a convincing decoy of himself standing still in the open, lets two drones waste their volley on it, and picks off the real targets while they reset. Nobody asked him to be efficient about it. He just is.
An actor drops character for one sentence mid-rescue: 'You kids actually showed up fast — better than last year.' Small, human, real. A seed.

npc_interactions.context: Observing from the control room throughout. Does not enter the arena.
npc_interactions.key_moment: Reads scores aloud after, flat, alphabetical. Pauses — not dramatically — after Yamaru's 1-B score. Continues. Nobody knows what the pause means. It means something.
npc_interactions.dm_dialogue: Scores. Class 1-A, exam sequence one. [reads alphabetically, no inflection]. Class 1-B reference score, posted for comparison: Yamaru Todao, eighty-four. You're all in.
npc_interactions.trigger: Any student who approaches him after gets one flat, accurate sentence. Not encouraging. Not discouraging. 'Your rescue time was poor. Work on civilian carry.' Or: 'The drone's weak point is visible at range. You didn't look.'

npc_interactions.context: At the arena gate before the exam, doing last-minute gear checks.
npc_interactions.key_moment: If a student approaches: she's already looking at their costume before they finish the sentence. 'Stand still.' Makes an adjustment they didn't ask for. It helps.
npc_interactions.dm_dialogue: On 1-B: 'Different site this year. Quieter, I heard. But thorough — Matsunami runs thorough.' She doesn't compare scores. She does note that Matsunami's been running Yamaru through sustained-damage drills for months. 'Interesting tactical choice.' Then her attention is elsewhere.
npc_interactions.trigger: Available before the exam. After, she's already reading medical reports for anyone who took a heavy hit from the Sentinel.

encounters.name: Drone Wave 1 — Initial Scatter
encounters.enemies: 6× Combat Drone Mk.I (2 per round, staggered)
encounters.terrain: Simulated urban block: three streets, two accessible buildings, debris fields, open plaza centre.
encounters.setup: Students dropped in from different entry points, 60+ ft apart. First drones target whoever's nearest.
encounters.tactics: No cooperation logic. Staggered arrival keeps pressure from spiking. Let students handle 1-2 solo before Mk.IIs appear.
encounters.rewards: 1 exam point per Mk.I destroyed, visible on the live leaderboard.

encounters.name: Drone Wave 2 — Heavy Support
encounters.enemies: 2× Combat Drone Mk.II, 4× Combat Drone Mk.I
encounters.terrain: Same arena. Debris from Wave 1 provides cover.
encounters.setup: Mk.IIs flank the heaviest combat area and acquire the highest-scoring student as target.
encounters.tactics: Mk.IIs use Missile Burst when 2+ students cluster. Mk.Is keep filling from the sides.

encounters.name: Wave 3 — Sentinel
encounters.terrain: Arena plaza centre — maximum open space.
encounters.setup: Drops with 'FINAL ASSESSMENT SEQUENCE INITIATED.' Worth 10 points split among the class — the incentive to coordinate.
encounters.tactics: Suppression Field on immediately. Railgun on the highest scorer. Stomp when students cluster. Phase Armour drops at 40 HP — the visible turning point.
encounters.rewards: 10 points split among students who dealt the final 20 HP.

foreshadowing: The rescue actor's line about response times slipping — port-adjacent incidents nobody's explaining.
Post-exam, Oshiro's earpiece buzzes once. He absorbs it, expression unchanged, and returns to the debrief.

Exam paperwork in the holding area includes a coverage report: a column for 'active incidents during exam window,' three entries, all marked resolved, resolution timestamps faster than any real response should be.
class1b_seeds: Results board shows 1-B's top score: Yamaru Todao, 84. Whether 1-A beats it depends on the session. Oshiro's reaction is silence either way — the difference is texture.
Fujisaki's aside about Matsunami running Yamaru through sustained-damage drills trails off before she finishes the thought.
Exam footage later posted to the internal board shows a split-screen with 1-B's site: quieter, more coordinated, fewer walls falling over.

arcs.name: Dorm Life Begins
arcs.summary: The class moves into Heights Alliance. No combat. Pure character chaos — this is how a class becomes a class instead of a results column.
arcs.dm_setup: Heights Alliance in the first week is burnt rice, an argument about whose turn it is to do dishes, and Zaro's fog drifting into a room a half-second before she does, startling someone new every other day. Toshida's speech bubble catches on a doorway again. Nakaya insists the toaster was already broken. These are small, and that's the whole point — this is where personality shows up without a quirk attached to it, and the best moments are the ones nobody scheduled: an unplanned late-night conversation, a rivalry starting over something as small as who gets the last of the good rice.

major_beats.name: Moving Day
major_beats.description: Arrivals at Heights Alliance. Common-space furniture claims are first-come-first-served. There will be an argument about the couch.
major_beats.dm_notes: Run as a montage unless a player wants a specific bit.

player_hooks.izuto: Done unpacking in three minutes flat, then spends the rest of the afternoon helping people who didn't ask — he doesn't know how to just sit with nothing to fix.
player_hooks.masahata: Arrives with a printed floor map and colour-coded furniture proposal. Nobody asked for this.
player_hooks.samitsu: Quietly claims the kitchen as his own territory within the hour. Nobody argues. Something already smells excellent.
player_hooks.kinosho: Her belongings fit in one small bag. Her room has a kettle and nothing else. She seems entirely satisfied by this.

major_beats.name: The Doorframe Incident
major_beats.description: Day one. Toshida is mid-sentence in the common room — not even shouting — and a word escapes with enough force to crack a doorframe panel loose.
major_beats.dm_notes: This is the icebreaker. Run it fast: the crack, the silence, Toshida's face, then go around the room for reactions.

player_hooks.toshida: Mortified but practiced — he's done this before, has an apology ready, fixes the panel himself. It falls out again the next morning. He has already, privately, named the doorframe Hiroshi, and has decided this is a rivalry now.

major_beats.name: The Charger Incident
major_beats.description: Day two. Nakaya notices Masahata's phone charger is dead and offers to fix it with a small controlled arc, purely as a favour. It works — technically. It also fuses the charging port shut at roughly double voltage, permanently.
major_beats.dm_notes: Pure comedy. Masahata is furious in a way that undercuts his usual self-importance, because the fix objectively worked. This is also the story the class tells reporters at the Sports Festival.

player_hooks.nakaya: Considers this an unambiguous success and is delighted every time someone brings it up, which is often.

major_beats.name: The Chart
major_beats.description: Day four. A laminated ranking chart appears on the fridge: entrance exam scores, a projected-rankings column, a 'Class 1-B benchmark' column, and 'Updated weekly' at the bottom. Nobody asked for this either.
major_beats.dm_notes: The chart is accurate, which is the actual problem. It survives the whole of Tier 1 accumulating coffee stains and re-lamination.

player_hooks.masahata: Keeps a second, more detailed version he shows no one unless directly asked. It has a column labelled only 'Other variables?' with a question mark and no elaboration.
player_hooks.ren: Listed as 'speed: high / rescue efficiency: low / improvement potential: significant.' Calls it wrong. Masahata says 'Empirically.' Ren points out that's not what the word means. Masahata says he knows what it means.

minor_beats: Zaro's first appearance in the common room is the fog before she is — someone nearly walks straight into a drift of deep purple haze in the corner, then jumps when a flat voice from inside it says: 'I was here first.'
Kinosho is found asleep in the stairwell between floors two and three. This becomes her primary spot. She has others. Nobody has catalogued them all.
First communal cooking attempt goes badly. Samitsu watches from the doorway, says nothing, and is in the kitchen unprompted the next night. Nobody has had a bad meal since.
Ichitaka projects a small hologram bird onto his own desk for no stated reason and lets it sit there for an hour before dismissing it. He doesn't explain. It looked like art.

Toragi leaves something small and useful — a pencil, a snack — on Yoshibara's desk with no note, then leaves before she notices. This happens three more times across the tier. She starts leaving him things back. Neither of them has said a word about it out loud.

Oshiro's room inspection: ninety seconds per room, silent, no warning. A notecard appears under every door before breakfast. Ren's says: 'You move fast when there's something to chase. Figure out what you're running toward.' He has no idea what to do with this.
Setaka mails three physical thank-you cards this week for entirely ordinary interactions. The recipients are unsettled in a way that becomes, over time, fond.

npc_interactions.key_moment: Notecards under doors before breakfast, never discussed in class, never explained.
npc_interactions.dm_dialogue: If caught in the hallway: 'Rooms. Not a request.' If asked about the notecards: 'You read it. Good.' Nothing more.
npc_interactions.trigger: Make each notecard land — something the specific student is actually working through, per their bio, not a generic compliment.

npc_interactions.context: Gear check visit, day two. Comes to see about dormitory-use costume adjustments. Stays three hours.
npc_interactions.key_moment: Yoshibara has extensive questions about whether her duplicate counts as a separate legal entity for gear-damage liability. Fujisaki is delighted. A very long conversation follows.
npc_interactions.dm_dialogue: To anyone nearby, mid-adjustment: 'Your left shoulder seam is going to go in about two weeks. Stand still.' Whether they asked or not.
npc_interactions.trigger: Any student who approaches gets a genuinely useful interaction.

npc_interactions.context: Cafeteria, next morning. Seated with Domoto at an adjacent table.
npc_interactions.key_moment: A full, unhurried survey of the 1-A table, taking exactly as long as he wants it to. Then he looks away. He's taken everything he needs from it.
npc_interactions.dm_dialogue: If approached: 'Yamaru. Class 1-B.' A firm single handshake. 'Good exam.' Returns to eating, unhurried. He considers this complete.
npc_interactions.trigger: Domoto, if present, winks and covers three seats in a single explosive hop while holding eye contact the whole way.

foreshadowing: Oshiro's notecard for Chozen: 'You notice what other people feel before they do. The city is going to need that more than the school does.' He doesn't know what this means yet — and it isn't strictly true the way he thinks it is; what he notices first is his own stress climbing, not anyone else's.
Common room TV, low volume: a small support agency for unlicensed quirk users in Kurogane Wharf has closed 'due to changing neighbourhood conditions.' Twelve seconds of airtime.

Hamagawa is visible through her office window one evening, reviewing a document headed 'Provisional Licensing Review — Kurogane Wharf Incidence Report Q3.' She closes it when she notices anyone looking.
class1b_seeds: 1-B's practice room is booked 6am Monday through Friday. They never cancel. The booking notes always name a specific drill objective.
Kagamo's 7am warmup blasts rattle the dorm twice. Masahata adds a row to the chart: 'Kagamo, Akake. Air Cannon. Notes: consistent.'

arcs.name: Capture the Flag
arcs.summary: Oshiro's opening combat class. Two teams, live stakes. Losing team runs extra laps; winners pick one perk. Rivalries get specific here.
arcs.dm_setup: Oshiro splits the teams himself, and his one rule — nobody fights their obvious counter — is what makes the matches interesting instead of predictable. Kazama ends up across from someone who can't just try to out-armor him directly. Ren ends up against a problem-solver like Izuto instead of someone he can simply outrun. The fun is watching people improvise around a matchup they didn't choose, not watching the 'correct' answer play out.

major_beats.name: Team Assignments
major_beats.description: Oshiro reads teams from a list. No explanation. Not random. No complaints taken.
major_beats.dm_notes: Split apart at least two students who'd naturally coordinate. Forced improvisation is the lesson.

player_hooks.masahata: Immediately identifies the optimal strategy for both teams — and is on the one his own analysis says should lose. Revises his strategy. The revision is also correct.

major_beats.name: First Blood
major_beats.description: Someone goes out early, and it's not who anyone predicted.
major_beats.dm_notes: Let it happen organically. If no PC, give it to a notable NPC — the 'safe pick' going down first resets everyone's assumptions.

major_beats.name: The Doubling Problem
major_beats.description: Yoshibara doubles. Both versions move toward the flag, identical in every visible way. The opposing team has to guess which to tag.
major_beats.dm_notes: Run both versions with the same base personality but let one be slightly bolder, one slightly more careful — a clue, not an answer.

player_hooks.chozen: This close to the flag, in front of the whole class, with real stakes — his stress is climbing whether he wants it to or not, and it's making him faster to commit to a read than he normally would be. He guesses. He's not totally sure why he's so sure.

major_beats.name: The Moment
major_beats.description: One unscripted decision changes the match.
major_beats.dm_notes: If nothing emerges naturally, give it to Kinosho — she was somewhere nobody expected, did something nobody saw coming, and won't explain herself after.

major_beats.name: The Exhale
major_beats.description: Oshiro announces results, flat, accurate, turns to leave. One student — probably whoever did something he didn't predict — gets a small exhale through his nose. He doesn't look back.
major_beats.dm_notes: Don't oversell it. If players miss it, someone comments later: 'Did Oshiro just... almost react?'

minor_beats: Masahata distributes a weakness analysis to his team the night before. His team splits up to 'optimise' and immediately stops communicating. His analysis was correct. Their execution wasn't.
Izuto's engine timing misfires at the worst moment — he overshoots the flag zone entirely. Audible.
Ren starts before the signal. Oshiro: 'Foul.' Hamagawa, consulting a rulebook that has no clear entry for this: 'Actually—' Oshiro overrules her. Points stand. Hamagawa makes a note anyway.

Zaro wins her matchup by portaling behind the flag line before anyone's finished scanning the field. Technically within the rules. Masahata's chart gets a correction: 'Quirk: Warp Gate, underweighted in initial analysis.'

npc_interactions.context: Running the match from the field edge. Never enters the arena.
npc_interactions.key_moment: Penalty calls delivered flat: 'Out.' No justification offered. The one exhale — see major beat 5.
npc_interactions.dm_dialogue: After the match: 'Losing team, laps in ten minutes. Winning team, see the schedule for perks. Everyone: what did you learn?' Doesn't wait for an answer.
npc_interactions.trigger: Students who bring a genuine post-match analysis get one sentence of acknowledgement each — the closest he gets to teaching voluntarily.

npc_interactions.key_moment: Nearly overrules Oshiro on the Ren signal-jump, doesn't, files it as 'Edge case: pre-signal movement. Review for provisional licensing impact.'
npc_interactions.dm_dialogue: Post-match, if approached: 'Yoshibara's duplication creates an unresolved identification problem under the provisional license framework — you can't technically tag a duplicate, it isn't the licensed individual. I've submitted a query. Don't tell her yet.'

npc_interactions.key_moment: An exaggerated double thumbs-up whenever the class does something impressive, delivered with her whole body. If Toshida's involved: the thumbs-up points at him specifically.
npc_interactions.dm_dialogue: None. Just present, watching, occasionally mouthing 'OKAY' at the glass.
npc_interactions.trigger: Only visible if students look at the window.

encounters.name: Capture the Flag — Class 1-A vs Class 1-A
encounters.enemies: NPC versions of the opposing student team — simplified stats: HP = 15 + (3 × level), AC = 11 + DEX mod, attack +3 to hit, 1d6 + STR/DEX damage.
encounters.terrain: Open training ground, four cover positions, two flag zones, one central choke point.
encounters.setup: Two-team capture the flag. Elimination by tag, HP-to-0, or a 3-second grapple hold. No lethal quirk use.
encounters.tactics: NPC students play to their actual character strengths — Yoshibara duplicates immediately, Zaro drops a fog shroud and pre-places a portal, Masahata executes his plan regardless of whether it's working.
encounters.rewards: Winning team picks: extended curfew, premium meals, priority training room access, or a reasonable player suggestion.

foreshadowing: Oshiro's earpiece activates mid-match. He absorbs it, keeps watching, doesn't leave. Something in Kurogane Wharf. He'll check after.

Hamagawa's legal query about Yoshibara's status has a smaller note underneath: 'Similar unresolved status exists for unlicensed quirk users operating under Ruin-adjacent organisations.' Nobody reads this except her.
The perk board gets an addition, probably from Masahata: 'Note: Class 1-B equivalent score — Hashige T., Yamaru T. flagged as exceptional. Source: Matsunami's office noticeboard, photographed.'
class1b_seeds: Oshiro's benchmark line: 'Class 1-B had three students who topped this score in their equivalent drill.' No names given. Masahata's chart gains three anonymous entries.
Kagamo's double thumbs-up, possibly aimed at Toshida specifically. Neither of them has said anything about it yet.
1-B's practice room board: 'Team Drill — Counterquirk Positioning' booked for Saturday, named for a technique that counters a known 1-A quirk pattern.

arcs.name: The Agency Visit
arcs.summary: Class 1-A assists a small hero agency in Kurogane Wharf for one day. Filing, crowd management, publicity. Then something goes wrong. Ruin appears for the first time — small, underdramatic, almost missable. That's the point.
arcs.dm_setup: Patchwork handles the villain encounter the way she'd handle a delayed bus — mildly annoyed, completely unsurprised — while the students are having the first real-world fight of their lives. That gap in reaction is the whole scene: she's seen this before, they haven't. The Ruin seed sitting nearby — a tag, a face, a name Hardskin won't finish saying — doesn't register as important in the moment. It's the kind of detail a player only recognizes later, when it comes back around.

major_beats.name: The Assignment
major_beats.description: Oshiro, zero ceremony: 'Agency visit. Kurogane Wharf. You're there by eight.' Patchwork Agency. Most students have never heard of it.
major_beats.dm_notes: The contrast with U.A.'s branding is intentional — Wharf agencies are workhorses. Masahata doesn't have a column for this agency. He makes one on the way there.

player_hooks.ren: Grew up here. Has opinions about the neighbourhood he hasn't shared with the class. He watched Patchwork work from the street when he was eleven, long before U.A. was a plan.

major_beats.name: A Quiet Tuesday
major_beats.description: Most of the day is filing, crowd management at a small community event, and photos with locals. A kid recognises someone from the entrance exam footage.
major_beats.dm_notes: Let this breathe. The mundane is the point — the class is used to adrenaline; a long, functional, boring morning is its own challenge.

player_hooks.ren: The neighbourhood knows him — not 'student at U.A.,' just 'the Suzuki kid.' Someone uses his first name. He doesn't correct them. The class notices.
player_hooks.aikawa: Reorganises the entire agency filing system without being asked. It's objectively better than what they had. They are mildly resentful and quietly grateful.
player_hooks.setaka: A kid asks him to lift a car for a photo. He explains, with complete sincerity, why that's not something he should do for fun in front of children, then does something small and impressive and appropriate instead. He writes the kid's name down.

major_beats.name: The Incident
major_beats.description: A street confrontation starts going wrong nearby. Patchwork is thirty seconds out. Students have to decide how to handle it before she arrives.
major_beats.dm_notes: Two Ruin Grunts and a Ruin Hardskin intimidating a shopkeeper — not overtly dramatic. Students who intervene face the first real villain encounter of the campaign. Both waiting and intervening are defensible; design the moment so neither is obviously correct.

player_hooks.ren: The shopkeeper is someone from his neighbourhood, by name. The 'wait for Patchwork' calculation takes no time at all.
player_hooks.izuto: A confined street means calibrating Engine output for collateral — a calculation he makes instinctively by now, without needing to think about it consciously.

major_beats.name: The Aftermath
major_beats.description: Patchwork arrives as it resolves. Direct, accurate, slightly alarming feedback — she's clocked everything.
major_beats.dm_notes: She doesn't say 'Ruin' outright yet if a student found the tattoo — she says 'affiliated.' If they missed it, she says nothing but makes a quiet call after they leave.

player_hooks.ren: Recognises her post-encounter twelve-second silence. He's seen her do this before. It means she's deciding what to leave out.

minor_beats: Izuto gets a crowd-control moment slightly wrong — activates Engine a half-second early, overshoots the mark, corrects. A photographer catches it. The caption reads 'Young Hero Overenthusiastic.' He does not find this funny.
A kid in the crowd has a Class 1-A poster from the entrance exam footage, too action-blurry to confirm who's actually in it, and asks for a signature anyway.
Among papers Aikawa reorganises: a follow-up flagged report — 'Quirk-for-hire operation, Kurogane Wharf, reference number PCR-7741.' The follow-up column is blank. Flagged eight months ago.
Patchwork, off-hand: 'The old rules about who goes where stopped applying about eighteen months ago. I don't know why. I just started noticing.'

npc_interactions.context: Agency hero, Kurogane Wharf. Eleven years here. Knows this neighbourhood the way structural engineers know buildings.
npc_interactions.key_moment: Post-encounter debrief, watching the subdued Grunts, not the students. 'The one who didn't run — the quiet one. That's a professional. Not local. You walked into someone's business trip, not their territory.' She stops there.
npc_interactions.dm_dialogue: On the neighbourhood: 'Eighteen months ago I started getting calls that resolved before I got there. Nobody wanted to talk. When your neighbourhood stops complaining to you, that's when you know something's changed.' On the students, specific to each: she's been watching since arrival and has an actual observation ready for anyone who approaches.

npc_interactions.context: The villain encounter. Doesn't talk much. Says nothing about Ruin when subdued. If asked about affiliation: 'I'm a freelancer.'
npc_interactions.key_moment: His fear when contained isn't fear of the students — it's fear of being seen. That gap is the important data.
npc_interactions.dm_dialogue: 'I just do pickup and delivery.' (Grunt line.) Hardskin, if pushed: 'You don't know what you're in the middle of.' He means the class. He's right.
npc_interactions.trigger: During and immediately after the encounter.

npc_interactions.context: Different agency, same district. Corridor encounter only.
npc_interactions.key_moment: Ten seconds. Precisely organised equipment cases, doesn't introduce himself, keeps walking. Name badge faces inward. If a student looks: Hashige, T., 1-B.
npc_interactions.dm_dialogue: If blocked: waits two seconds, moves around with minimum displacement. If addressed: 'Excuse me.' Keeps walking.
npc_interactions.trigger: One brief crossing during the visit.

encounters.name: Street Confrontation — Ruin Operatives
encounters.terrain: Kurogane Wharf street, 15ft wide, buildings both sides, one shopfront, one alley exit north. Civilians scatter round 1.
encounters.setup: Grunts visibly intimidating a shopkeeper. Hardskin holds back ten feet, watching. Six seconds before Patchwork arrives.
encounters.tactics: Grunts engage if challenged. Hardskin waits one round then joins, coordinating with Pack Fighter. Goes for whoever looks most capable. Grunts surrender at 5 HP; Hardskin takes the hit silently.
encounters.dm_notes: Tattoo visible on DC 15 Perception, DC 12 on a subdued target. Whether the class finds it shapes how much context they carry into Tier 2 — both outcomes are valid.
encounters.rewards: No material reward. Patchwork's feedback and the blank follow-up column are the actual payoff.

foreshadowing: PCR-7741, the blank follow-up report. Describes a quirk-for-hire network out of three Kurogane Wharf businesses. Never assigned. Original filer transferred.
The Hardskin's disproportionate fear of being identified. Whoever he answers to has enough reach that getting caught by student heroes should be minor and clearly isn't.
Patchwork's eighteen-month timeline lines up exactly with the founding of Ruin's first Wharf operation, which the students can't date until Tier 3. When they can, they'll remember this conversation.
Ren notices a gear-consulting shop he used as a kid is dark now, replaced by something Ruin-adjacent. He doesn't know that yet.
class1b_seeds: A crowd-management civilian recognises a 1-A student from the exam footage. Asked about 1-B: 'Different site. I heard their scores were better in some areas.' No more detail than that.
Hashige's corridor crossing. Precision as a personality trait, visible even in ten seconds.
